events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Coastal waters from Florence to Cape Blanco OR out 10 nm; Waters from Florence to Cape Blanco OR from 10 to 60 nm
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...South winds 25 to 35 kt with gusts up to 40 kt and very
steep and hazardous, chaotic seas building to 25 to 30 ft at
19 seconds this evening. Then, tonight into Saturday morning,
southwest winds 20 to 30 kt tonight with very steep and
hazardous seas 25 to 30 ft at 18 seconds. Saturday afternoon
and evening, south winds 35 to 45 kt with gusts 55 to 60 kt
and seas 19 to 25 ft at 16 seconds expected.

* WHERE...All the area.

* WHEN...For the Gale Warning, until 7 PM PST this evening. For
the Hazardous Seas Warning, from 7 PM this evening to 1 PM PST
Saturday. For the Storm Warning, from 1 PM Saturday to 1 AM
PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Very strong winds and very steep seas could capsize
or damage vessels. Visibilities will be significantly reduced.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Another strong front will move in late
Saturday and Saturday night with the potential for storm force
winds and very steep and hazardous seas. This front will be
followed by another round of very high westerly swell Sunday
into Monday. Please continue to monitor the forecast for
updates on this high impact weather pattern.

grouped_sources.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Avery; Madison; Yancey; Mitchell; Swain; Haywood; Graham
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Periods of snow showers will continue through tonight across the
higher elevations of the North Carolina mountain counties along
the Tennessee border. Snow accumulations of up to 2 inches can be
expected, mainly above 3500 feet. Locally higher amounts are
expected mainly above 5000 feet. Lower elevation areas may see
some snow showers but no significant accumulations are expected.
Wind gusts up to 35 mph are also expected.

If you will be traveling any higher elevation roadways, be alert
for slippery road conditions and gusty winds.

events.region: Apalachee Bay or Coastal Waters From Keaton Beach to Ochlockonee River Fl out to 20 Nm; Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach out 20 NM; Coastal Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola out 20 NM; Coastal Waters From  Ochlockonee River to Apalachicola FL out to 20 Nm; Coastal waters from  Suwannee River to Keaton Beach out 20 NM; Waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach from 20 to 60 NM; Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM; Waters from Suwannee River to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...North winds near 20 kt with gusts up to 25 kt expected.

* WHERE...Offshore Gulf waters from the Walton-Okaloosa County
line to the Ochlockonee River from 20 to 60 nautical miles
out, Nearshore Gulf waters from the Ochlockonee River to the
Suwannee River out 20 nautical miles, Coastal waters from
Mexico Beach to Okaloosa Walton County Line FL out 20 NM,
Coastal waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola FL out 20 NM,
and Coastal Waters From Ochlockonee River to Apalachicola Fl
out to 20 Nm.

* WHEN...Until 8 AM EST /7 AM CST/ Saturday.

* IMPACTS...A Small Craft Advisory means that wind speeds of 20
to 33 knots, or seas of 7 feet or greater, are expected to
produce hazardous conditions for small craft. These hazardous
conditions may result in poor vessel handling and steering
response, broaching, overturned dinghies and kayaks, slips and
falls on slippery decks, rub damage along docks and seawalls,
and dragging anchors.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Guam; Rota; Tinian; Saipan
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 7 to 9 feet in the surf zone.
Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...North facing reefs of the Marianas.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM ChST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The long-period north swell that originated
from Typhoon Cempaka has most likely peaked yesterday, but could
take time to subside. Therefore, large surf and dangerous rip
currents will likely continue through this afternoon.
